title: staging proof attempts inherit earlier passes' branches: clear origins
body:
agent-faults-staging.ts keys each attempt's /proof/git origin by attempt name in Durable Object storage, which outlives a pass; its reclaim destroys the container but not the origin, and /proof/start's init() keeps existing storage. A second run of the proof against the same deployment therefore boots each attempt on the previous pass's pushed branch. Observed this attempt: an intermediate second run failed 'the tool did not run twice' because the first run's tool-runs.txt (one line) rode the second run's boot and the model's own append made two — the host's reattach itself was sound. The recorded pass ran on a fresh deployment, and the README now warns to run once per deployment, but that is prose. Worth a tick: make each proof pass self-cleaning — reclaim clears the attempt's origin, or start resets it — so the proof cannot silently inherit.
evidence: harness/proof/agent-faults-staging.ts (reclaim, after the evidence read); cloudflare/src/staging-agent.ts (/proof/start -> origins.get(...).init(token), keeping prior storage); this attempt's intermediate run: evidence tool_runs_file read 'tool-ran-once\ntool-ran-once\n' while the log shows the sleep command issued exactly once
